record.original_question: For every polygon with n vertices and h holes, can the entire polygon be illuminated by at most floor((n+h)/3) vertex guards, where a vertex guard is placed at a polygon vertex and can illuminate in all directions from that point?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 Any polygon with n vertices and h holes can be illuminated with b n+h 3 c vertex guards.
In this case, the guards can illuminate all around themselves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon with h polygonal holes, with n vertices in total (counting vertices on the outer boundary and on all hole boundaries). A vertex guard is a point placed at a vertex of P (on the outer boundary or on a hole boundary) which illuminates every point q in the closed region of P such that the open line segment from the guard to q lies in the interior of P (equivalently, the guard sees q). The polygon is said to be illuminated by a set of vertex guards if every point of the closed region of P (with holes removed) is seen by at least one guard.

Prove or disprove: for every such polygon P with n vertices and h holes, there exists a set of at most ⌊(n+h)/3⌋ vertex guards that illuminates the entire polygon.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing conjecture (attributed to Shermer) on vertex guards for polygons with holes. It is known to hold for h = 1 (proved independently by Shermer and by Aggarwal). For general h, the conjecture remains open; recent work (e.g., Alipour, 2021) only establishes related partial results such as guarding all vertices and the outer boundary with ⌊(n+h)/3⌋ vertex guards.

status_evidence.title: On guarding polygons with holes (arXiv:2102.10317)
status_evidence.snippet: There is an old conjecture by Shermer that ⌊(n+h)/3⌋ vertex guards are sufficient... proved for h=1 by Shermer and Aggarwal; the general case remains unproven.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open for general h; only h=1 case is settled.

status_evidence.title: Illumination of Polygons (Urrutia open problems)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on illumination/guarding of polygons including vertex guards in polygons with holes.
